task: Core #1186 F6-U03m: genuine Docker PG17 Office-wide catalog RLS/ACL/trigger inventory with fail-closed release blockers

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical read-only native PG17 catalog-wide inventory, with real SQL source identity. Separate machine observations from expert interpretation; unresolved findings block release, and no SQL or production authority is modified.

acceptanceCriteria: Unchanged source-verified 59+19 original SQL and original target-preflight, target-postflight and COMMIT reproduced on identity-verified disposable Docker PG17.

Read-only native query covers every public/private application base/partitioned table, every catalog policy and its role names/USING/WITH CHECK, all public/private functions and effective anon/authenticated/service_role/PUBLIC EXECUTE, and non-internal triggers with enablement.

Catalog is machine JSON, has stable object inventory hash, minimum observed constraints 190 public tables, 379 public functions, 129 public policies from F6-U03l and includes exact v2/v3 results with required deny/allow.
Audit emits every conservative Office-relevant object, actionable finding details and evidence; never auto-confirms arbitrary RLS/SECURITY DEFINER semantics as secure.
Negative tests show absent/garbled catalog, missing mandated v2/v3 function, malformed role grant, disabled RLS, exposed SECURITY DEFINER and missing source identity fail/flag correctly.

Always release BLOCKED pending full semantic Office policy/ACL/RPC supersession review, signed-in tenant JWT Alap/Pro, managed provider Auth/Storage and approved migration package, even with zero findings.
Exact-head source proof, quality, TS/build, Security Audit, Completion Truth and Lifecycle pass for inventory diagnostic only.

Every related catalog relation/function reports native anon/authenticated schema USAGE, and exposed privileged-function high signal requires both matching role function EXECUTE and schema USAGE; ACL-only cases get review severity.
Native pg_proc catalog identifies trigger-returning functions, and negative test differentiates trigger helper ACL review from genuinely callable SECURITY DEFINER with authenticated schema USAGE.
invariants: All 78 historical Git-pinned source bytes untouched; native SELECT-only catalog executes after real original PostgreSQL17 COMMIT.
No app-owned SQL writes through audit; only original F6-U03k fixture executed locally.
PG peer IP/DB/user/version must prove local actual Docker service; reject all inherited external libpq selectors.
Database role privilege from superuser is not a substitute for browser/service_role privilege, and PUBLIC default grants must be visible.
No auth/tenant provider or hosted release gate can be marked proven from catalog inventory.
Any incomplete schema or missing expected object counts fails exact diagnostic instead of underreporting possible risk.
forbiddenStates: Any catalog snapshot silently excludes public/private Office tables or policies while claiming complete source coverage.
An exposed SECURITY DEFINER candidate to PUBLIC/anon/authenticated is automatically marked safe on basis of naming alone.
An RLS-disabled Office-related relation is hidden, or update policy without explicit WITH CHECK is reported a confirmed defect without interpretation.
A read-only query runs on a hosted database or takes credentials/project selectors from environment.
Generated report claims `releaseAuthorized=true` or that signed-in Alap/Pro/managed Auth/Storage are proven.
The original 78 SQL or hosted abort-before-DROP is edited to pass the audit.

failureModes: New function or table introduced by one original source falls outside narrow office_ pattern but references Office tables via procedure SQL.
Catalog query filters policies by role OIDs and misreports Supabase role names because Docker OIDs differ.
Default PUBLIC EXECUTE on a SECURITY DEFINER may bypass absence of explicit anon GRANT.
A changed trigger enablement is overlooked if test only counts trigger names.
Missing UPDATE WITH CHECK is misclassified as unconditional authorization bypass when PostgreSQL uses USING fallback.
Postflight fails but catalog query still executes against old snapshot.
Read-only SQL errors are swallowed by shell and generated JSON report is empty but green.
edgeCases: pg_get_functiondef for C/extension routines cannot be treated as SQL text; use language/source search only as conservative relevance hint.
Both partitioned relation relkind p and ordinary r count as tables; avoid treating indexes as tables.
policy `polwithcheck` nullable and pg_get_expr nullable: preserve null rather than infer TRUE.
Role list includes OID zero for PUBLIC; render role names deterministically rather than raw OID.
Trigger tgenabled values O/D/R/A have different semantics; report D as disabled, R as replica-only not always-on.
Object lists may be long: capture catalog JSON artifact with deterministic sorting, fail on missing mandatory object counts.

specialistReviews.finding: A mechanically green catalog scanner cannot prove all policy predicate semantics or real signed-in tenant identity.
specialistReviews.resolution: Label findings as review indications and always block release until explicit manual+tenant/provider proofs; include raw RLS expressions for later review.

specialistReviews.finding: Policies may be attached to partitioned relations; only `pg_policy` joined to simple tables can be incomplete.
specialistReviews.resolution: Include pg_class relkind r,p and all pg_policy public/private objects, policy role normalization and trigger enablement.

specialistReviews.finding: Local source replay plus audit may be mistaken for approved 78-source hosted migration package.
specialistReviews.resolution: Source review candidate only; releaseAuthorized false and blocked known acceptance fields mandatory.

specialistReviews.finding: Duplicated catalog compiler would create parallel authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Reuse existing original F6-U03k SQL composer, candidate F6-U03l source and separate read-only audit query only, no change to original hosted guard.

challenge.scenario: A public SECURITY DEFINER RPC has default PUBLIC EXECUTE but source SQL contains no explicit anon grant.
challenge.finding: Static grep reports no privilege while effective native Postgres permissions permit browser calls.
challenge.resolution: Query `has_function_privilege` for actual anon/authenticated/service_role and proacl PUBLIC on every app function; flag exposed relevant definer for review.

challenge.scenario: A public/private Office table has rowsecurity disabled yet a policy of the same name exists elsewhere.
challenge.finding: Policy count does not prove RLS enabled on actual Office relation.
challenge.resolution: Pair pg_class.relrowsecurity/relforcerowsecurity with exact relation OID, report table and effective role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE.

challenge.scenario: RLS UPDATE policy omits explicit WITH CHECK; naive checker calls a confirmed cross-tenant write.
challenge.finding: PostgreSQL may use USING fallback; diagnosing exploit from null polwithcheck is false certainty.
challenge.resolution: Emit review finding with null withCheck, explicit classification and no automatic exploit proof.

challenge.scenario: A trigger exists but is disabled or replica-only, invalidating Office integrity hook behavior.
challenge.finding: Trigger-name counts look green while write-time audit/tenant boundary may not execute.
challenge.resolution: Query actual pg_trigger.tgenabled and flag D and R for Office-relevant tables.

challenge.scenario: Some Office function uses a generic helper name but references office_ tables in PLpgSQL source.
challenge.finding: Simple office_ prefix audit omits helper and its effective EXECUTE exposure.
challenge.resolution: Conservatively include function source text relevance marker for office/team/communication patterns and retain full catalog objects and counts for manual review.

challenge.scenario: Missing SQL or failed COMMIT causes catalog JSON of 0 objects to pass because the checker only validates shape.
challenge.finding: False-green lifecycle could approve uninstalled Office schema.
challenge.resolution: Enforce psql ON_ERROR_STOP=1, original postflight and COMMIT, independent source 78 identities and minimum previously observed catalog counts; fail-closed on empty/incomplete JSON.

challenge.scenario: One role name in policy is serialized as a different OID in managed Supabase than local fixture.
challenge.finding: Comparing raw role OIDs produces misleading drift and possibly invalid release classification.
challenge.resolution: Resolve policy roles through pg_roles to readable role names and explicitly preserve PUBLIC role 0; native catalog counts valid only locally.

challenge.scenario: A green local audit report is used as proof of actual authenticated Alap/Pro JWT tenant isolation and managed Auth/Storage.
challenge.finding: A real provider claim without signed-in tenant request evidence violates source-scoped Truth contract.
challenge.resolution: Machine verdict release_BLOCKED, providerManagedProven=false, signedInAlapProRlsProven=false, hostedTouched=false, and document next authority.

challenge.scenario: A private-schema SECURITY DEFINER has effective EXECUTE for anon but no USAGE on its private namespace, and is classified as directly browser-exposable.
challenge.finding: Function EXECUTE alone is not a callable API: PostgreSQL requires schema USAGE, and provider Data API schema exposure is another independent gate. An unconditional HIGH finding is a false positive.
challenge.resolution: Query has_schema_privilege for each table/function namespace, classify high direct exposure only when schema USAGE and role EXECUTE are both true; retain ACL-only as REVIEW_REQUIRED and provider exposure separate.

challenge.scenario: A native PostgreSQL trigger-returning helper (prorettype trigger) has EXECUTE to PUBLIC/authenticated with private schema USAGE and is marked as directly callable SECURITY DEFINER RPC.
challenge.finding: PostgreSQL trigger functions can only run as triggers; routine-level EXECUTE metadata is not sufficient to classify direct SQL invocation as a browser RPC entrypoint.
challenge.resolution: Collect function return type from pg_proc, classify `RETURNS trigger` function as trigger-only ACL review and never as direct-browser SQL RPC even with schema USAGE; separately review the enabled trigger and source integrity.

proofPlan: Run canonical exact-scope Development Guard, read all 45 active Known Failures and risk/authority challenges; critical Plan Before Code PASS before audit implementation.

Run native read-only public/private catalog SELECT for all tables, policy normalized role names/expressions, functions effective execute rights, triggers and enabled states; preserve full raw JSON.
Adversarial negative Vitest against absent object, default PUBLIC grant, RLS-disabled table, disabled trigger and misclassified UPDATE check.
Evidence reports scoped local catalog and release BLOCKED even if all specific findings reviewed, exact-head CI/Truth/Lifecycle.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: F6-U03l locally source-pinned all 78 SQL sources and proved exact legacy inbound v2/v3 ACL after true PostgreSQL17 COMMIT. The 78-file local candidate has no full Office-wide RLS/ACL/trigger/supersession inventory; a narrow two-function ACL check cannot prove other Office functions and policies safe. Need complete machine-readable native catalog evidence for all app relations, policies, public/private function effective privileges and triggers, a conservative Office relevance classifier, risk findings and independently reviewed release blockers. No provider or tenant authentication acceptance follows.
observableOutcomes: After exact source-authentic F6-U03k 78-file PostgreSQL17 COMMIT + original preflight/postflight, issue read-only pg_catalog SQL returning structured data for *all* public/private relations, pg_policy definitions and role names, function signatures/SECURITY DEFINER/effective execute grants, and triggers/enablement.

Produce deterministic Office-scope audit from actual catalog and explicit policy/grant/relevance evidence, retain full object counts and stable SHA256. No synthetic Office relations or modifying SQL in proof.

Emit machine findings for RLS-disabled Office relations, SECURITY DEFINER reachable by browser/PUBLIC or elevated role, suspicious broad table grants, disabled Office triggers and missing explicit UPDATE WITH CHECK; classify uncertain patterns as REVIEW_REQUIRED, not automatically proven vulnerability.
Fail closed on absent, malformed, incomplete, forged or contradictory native PG17 evidence; raw JSON evidence stored with final machine findings and source candidate version.
Preserve explicit releaseAuthorized=false, hostedTouched=false, jwtTenantRlsProven=false, providerManagedProven=false even if diagnostic CI is SUCCESS.
Exact-head independent Docker17 proof, negative Vitest, source provenance, normal CI, Truth and Lifecycle pass for scoped diagnostic only.
Distinguish effective object/function EXECUTE grants from schema USAGE for anon/authenticated, and do not label private SECURITY DEFINER high-risk direct browser exposure without namespace USAGE.
Function catalog must include native PostgreSQL trigger-return signature flag; high direct-RPC exposure excludes trigger functions (which cannot be invoked directly).
unresolvedRisks: Native Docker roles are fixture roles, not real Supabase JWT sessions; authenticated/Alap/Pro row-boundary tests remain blocked.
Function code and RLS policy semantics cannot be proven secure by regex, row counts or static SQL metadata; human/semantic review remains mandatory.
All public/private data schema includes objects unrelated to Office; audit must retain full counts while Office relevance is conservative and explicit.
A policy UPDATE without explicit WITH CHECK can inherit USING semantics under PostgreSQL; report review signal not automatic exploitable vulnerability.
Historical Supabase security definer function code may call role-dependent helpers and provider Auth/Storage; local successful schema install cannot cover managed behavior.
PostgreSQL schema USAGE alone does not confirm Supabase Data API exposure; hosted schema exposure settings must be reviewed separately.
